qualification: Local uncommitted namespace experiment and paper update; no exact-commit remote CI, independent administration, release or breakthrough qualification.
limits: The host kernel, operator, launcher and brokers remain trusted. Namespace and selected path probes do not qualify all kernel escapes, independent administration or production credentials.
Both gates share the same isolation layer, kernel host, native verifier, graph adapters and courier; this is an outcome-gate comparison, not complete protocol equivalence.

The trusted host constructs adversarial RPCs and injects receiver faults. Normal and replacement couriers and all receiver operations run isolated. The probe is a fixed executable, not arbitrary attacker code.
A receiver can intentionally read its own key at /receiver/key.seed. Denied original host paths do not imply that its own mounted key is inaccessible to it.
All twenty SIGKILL fault checks observe launcher descendants stop, using original PID start times. Terminated zombies count as stopped; host reaping is not asserted.
No seccomp filter or aggregate CPU, memory, process and disk quotas; bounded frames and waits alone do not qualify denial-of-service resistance.
Static native capability-policy data and fixed logical clock; no live model, proposed executable, remote transport, host power loss or database cloning test.
Claimed effects without results preserve uncertainty. The fixture does not replay them or export successor success evidence.
Public configuration and signed traces are retained. Private seeds, binary databases and socket files are excluded. Socket brokers do not persist after the run.
All measured outcomes match the independent ledger. No latency, integration-cost, storage-cost or intervention advantage was measured.
